free_text.inst.v2.D8: Completed strictly as a biographical exercise from the public record: no reading, chart or verdict was viewed, so Part D's questions about a reading (D1-D7) were left unanswered rather than invented. Where the record is genuinely contested - the exact finalisation of the first divorce, the childhood appendectomy, how much credit is 'deserved' - the answer given is the one a careful biographer could defend from published sources, and the notes field records the reasoning.

notes: Sources: the long-form birth certificate released April 2011 (Jamaica Hospital, Queens, New York, 14 June 1946, 10:54 a.m.), standard biographies (Blair, D'Antonio, Kranish/Fisher), the New York Times' 2018 investigation of the family finances, court and SEC filings, and White House physicians' letters. A1/A2: the 10:54 a.m. time comes from the released certificate and is stated to the minute, so 'certificate' + 'exact'; astrologers have proposed rectifications but no correction is part of the record he himself holds, hence A3 'no'. A4: counted the Walter Reed COVID-19 admission (October 2020), emergency treatment after the Butler shooting (13 July 2024), and the childhood appendectomy reported in the biographies. A5: 'one' rests on that reported appendectomy; his heel bone spurs were not operated on. A6: documented recurring issues are cardiovascular (statin therapy, elevated coronary calcium score reported by his physicians in 2018) and the legs/feet (the 1968 heel bone-spur deferment and the chronic venous insufficiency disclosed in July 2025). A9 'mixed': Friedrich Trump died at 49 in the 1918 influenza pandemic while Mary Anne MacLeod's parents lived to 88 and 96 and Elizabeth Christ Trump to 85 - an average near 80 that hides a very wide spread. A13: Fred Jr. died in 1981, so 'lost'. A14: BS in economics, Wharton School, 1968, after two years at Fordham - a transfer, not an interruption (A15 'no'). A16: own business throughout, plus a government salary as president in two terms (he declined or donated the salary, but the office is a public-body post). A19 'short' records his own long-documented and repeatedly stated position that he is given less credit than his work warrants; 'about right' is arguable given the scale of his public recognition. A21 'net_gain': the publicly traded casino company lost its shareholders money, but his personal holdings - most conspicuously the DJT stake - have been a large paper gain. A22 'significant': the 2018 New York Times investigation documented at least $413m (in then-current dollars) received from his father's businesses. A23 'serious_past': the early-1990s crisis, when he was personally liable for roughly $900m, is the clearest case; the 2024 New York civil-fraud penalty was thrown out by the Appellate Division in August 2025. A25: 1977 is the first marriage (Ivana Zelnickova, 7 April 1977); the later two are in A35. A27 'mixed': two divorces and a third marriage now in its third decade. A28: five children - Donald Jr. (1977), Ivanka (1981), Eric (1984), Tiffany (1993), Barron (2006). A31 'no': there is no public record of treatment for depression or anxiety. A32 'mild': Presbyterian upbringing and the influence of Norman Vincent Peale, but no documented regular practice. A33 'over5': Philadelphia for Wharton, Washington for two presidencies, and Palm Beach as his declared primary residence since 2019. A34 'extended': five years boarding at the New York Military Academy, 1959-1964. A35: the divorce from Ivana is dated to the December 1990 decree; the financial settlement ran on and is often cited as finalising in 1992. The four corporate Chapter 11 filings are the Taj Mahal (July 1991), the Plaza Hotel (November 1992), Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts (November 2004) and Trump Entertainment Resorts (February 2009). June 1999 carries both the Marla Maples divorce decree and Fred Sr.'s death. A36 'much_better': he won the 2024 election and returned to office, against six preceding years that included an election defeat, two impeachments, four indictments and a felony conviction. B3 'younger' follows the frequent public commentary on his apparent age, and is the least certain answer in Part B. B4 'middle': fourth of five, after Maryanne, Fred Jr. and Elizabeth and before Robert. C1 'difficulty' rests on two divorces; C5 'gone well' on the inheritance, which is the best-documented item in the whole form (confidence 5). C9 was scored as difficulty on the sheer volume of sustained organised opposition and litigation, even though he has more often than not prevailed. C11 was given confidence 2 - the inner life is the area on which the public record says least. Part D (D1-D7) omitted: those questions ask about a reading, which this exercise did not view.
